lectures.title: The Problem with Discretionary Access Control

cues.en: So what's the problem with discretionary access control?
Well, the problem is when our application does something that we did not intended it to do, and then
it can just do anything that those permissions allow our application.
So if our application only executes code in a way that we thought about, then everything is okay and
discretionary access control is enough.
But we should not always expect this to be the case.
There might be backs in our code, there might be backs in libraries that we use, there might be configuration
problems, and thus it's best to assume that people will be able to break into our application.
And we should assume that at some point people or attackers might be able to execute arbitrary code
on our system.

behave in a way that we didn't intended our application to be.
